walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why might managed retreat be more sustainable than building a sea wall?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Sea walls always solve coastal erosion problems permanently.
Sea walls are expensive, deflect erosion elsewhere and reflect wave energy worsening beach loss; managed retreat works with natural processes, creates habitat and is cheaper long-term.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
Choropleth maps are for showing churches and isoline maps are for showing roads.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a choropleth and an isoline map?
options: Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
Choropleth maps are for showing churches and isoline maps are for showing roads.
Choropleths use coloured/shaded areas to show data values per region (e.g. population density by county); isoline maps use lines connecting points of equal value (e.g. contours, isobars).
Choropleth and isoline maps are the same thing.
